brief.headline: Memory supercycle intact: Q2 consensus tops ₩150tn combined OP, DDR5 margins now exceed HBM, CoWoS sold out through 2026
brief.summary: <cite index="40-5,40-6">Consensus projects Samsung and SK Hynix combined Q2 operating profit exceeding ₩150 trillion, with Samsung at ₩88.3 trillion revenue and SK Hynix at ₩64.3 trillion OP.</cite> <cite index="4-1,4-10">Conventional DRAM margins now reportedly reach ~80% vs HBM at ~60%, reversing prior narratives, as DDR5 spot pricing remains structurally elevated.</cite> <cite index="12-7,12-8">DRAM contract prices rose 58-63% QoQ in Q2 2026 following a 90-95% surge in Q1, while NAND jumped 70-75% QoQ.</cite> <cite index="33-7,33-11">CoWoS capacity remains sold out through 2025 and into 2026, with assembly capacity oversubscribed through at least mid-2026.</cite> <cite index="22-5,22-9">Hyperscalers collectively guided ~$700 billion 2026 capex, nearly double 2025, sustaining HBM and enterprise DRAM demand.</cite>
brief.pair_trade_view: Short-term tactical edge to Samsung on revenue scale and commodity DRAM exposure to persistent supply tightness; SK Hynix retains structural margin premium (~72% Q1 OP margin vs Samsung Device Solutions ~95% of total OP) via HBM dominance. <cite index="47-2,47-10,47-11">Samsung led Q1 DRAM share at 38.6% vs SK Hynix 28.8%, with Samsung revenue up 95.4% vs market 85.3%.</cite> <cite index="47-21,47-22">SK Hynix HBM market share ~57%, delivered Q1 OP margin ~72%, well above Samsung.</cite> <cite index="45-1,45-3,45-4">Both names sold off sharply June 8-10: KOSPI fell 8.3%, Samsung down >10% intraday, SK Hynix -7-8%, erasing weeks of gains on AI valuation fears.</cite> Near-term risk/reward skewed to Samsung on valuation reset and DDR5 margin tailwind; hold SK Hynix for HBM4 ramp into H2 and AI server LTAs. Watch for packaging capex announcements and regional investment disclosure at June presidential roundtable.

memory_cycle.notes: <cite index="3-13,16-20,16-21">DRAM prices not expected to peak until at least 2026, with prices expected to remain high through 2028 as new fab capacity unlikely before late 2027.</cite> <cite index="14-5,14-6">Samsung and SK Hynix, controlling ~70% global DRAM, signaled no aggressive capacity expansion, prioritizing profitability over volume.</cite> <cite index="17-6,17-7,17-8">Supplier inventories remain low, maintaining strong pricing power; PC DRAM contract prices grew significantly in Q2, with upward trend projected into Q3 and Q4, though momentum slowing.</cite> Structural rather than cyclical: HBM consuming 3x wafer capacity per GB vs DDR5, advanced packaging bottleneck persists, hyperscaler LTAs locking in multi-year allocations.

brief.hbm_pulse: <cite index="5-1,5-2">HBM3E prices increased ~20% for 2026 deliveries, with supply remaining tight as Samsung and SK Hynix prioritize ramping HBM4 production.</cite> <cite index="9-4,9-11">HBM3 ~$200/stack, HBM3E ~$300/stack, HBM4 ~$500/stack; lead times for HBM3E remain 20-26 weeks.</cite> <cite index="9-7,9-8">HBM now represents 30-40% of total AI accelerator BOM, up from <20% two generations ago; B200 HBM alone costs $2,400, exceeding logic die.</cite> <cite index="34-7">HBM3e and HBM4 supply from Samsung and SK Hynix struggling to keep pace, creating dual-constraint environment with CoWoS.</cite> <cite index="40-8">Samsung unveiled next-gen HBM4 memory, aiming to tighten grip on AI accelerators.</cite> SK Hynix holds ~53% HBM market Q3 2025 vs Samsung 35%, but gap narrowing as Samsung HBM4 reportedly passed Broadcom tests for Google TPU.

news_pulse.headline: Samsung, SK Hynix Q2 combined OP consensus tops ₩150tn on memory boom
news_pulse.implication: Record earnings driven by AI memory demand and surging margins across DRAM/NAND/HBM; validates sustained pricing power through H1.

news_pulse.headline: DDR5 margins reportedly surpass HBM at ~80% vs ~60%
news_pulse.implication: Conventional DRAM pricing strength exceeds HBM premium; Samsung benefits from broader commodity exposure, SK Hynix pricing strategy under scrutiny.

news_pulse.headline: KOSPI crashes 8.3%, Samsung -10%+ intraday, SK Hynix -7-8% on AI valuation fears
news_pulse.implication: Sharp multiple compression erases weeks of gains; risk-off triggered by US rate expectations and AI bubble concerns despite strong fundamentals.

news_pulse.headline: Hyperscaler 2026 capex revised to ~$700bn, up ~69% YoY
news_pulse.implication: Sustained demand backdrop for HBM, enterprise DRAM, and SSDs; Microsoft +24% to $190bn, Amazon $200bn, Alphabet $185bn, Meta $125-145bn.

news_pulse.headline: TSMC CoWoS sold out through 2025 and into 2026, capacity 35k→130k wpm by end-2026
news_pulse.implication: Advanced packaging remains primary constraint on AI accelerator supply; NVIDIA secured 60-70% allocation, limiting AMD/hyperscaler custom silicon.

news_pulse.headline: DRAM contract prices +58-63% QoQ Q2, NAND +70-75% following Q1 gains of 90-95% and 55-60%
news_pulse.implication: Pricing momentum moderating but still extreme; server DRAM >60% QoQ, enterprise SSD demand absorbing NAND capacity, client markets rationed.

news_pulse.headline: Samsung leads Q1 DRAM share 38.6% vs SK Hynix 28.8%, but SK Hynix Q1 OP margin ~72% vs Samsung lower
news_pulse.implication: Samsung regained revenue crown via commodity/server DRAM scale; SK Hynix retains profitability edge via HBM mix at ~57% market share.

news_pulse.headline: Samsung, SK Hynix floated for new packaging facilities in Korea southwest (Gwangju); no decision confirmed
news_pulse.implication: Potential June disclosure at presidential roundtable; SK Hynix already building P&T7 in Cheongju (₩19tn); Samsung Onyang/Cheonan expansion eyed.

brief.derivatives_signal: KOSPI volatility spiked; circuit breakers triggered June 8. Both names trading at steep discounts to recent highs despite record earnings trajectory. Options markets pricing elevated near-term vol; watch for stabilization around Q2 earnings guidance (late July). ADR spreads widened on overnight selloff.
